# Scaling a two-limb number by a power of two

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_pow2_2_full` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$x c$ with results like those of `T` for infinite and NaN operands and on overflow: the result of its core, [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md), when that is finite, and otherwise a canonical infinity or NaN:

$$w \approx x c.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $w = w_0 + w_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ldexp(x, n)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `int` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $c = 2^n$, for every `n`: when $2^n$ is not a number of `T`, two or three calls, whose composition is argued and tested but not machine-checked ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values)); `constexpr`, the steps included, with the same values in constant evaluation ([the rule of the product](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); rounds |
| `half(x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $c = 1/2$; `constexpr`, the steps included, with the same values in constant evaluation ([the rule of the product](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); rounds |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $x$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- $c$ is a finite power of two: $c = 2^n$ for an integer $n$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **F1.** $w$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- **F2.** If $w_0$ is finite, then every operand is finite and $w$ satisfies the statement of its core, [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md):
    - $w$ is normalized: $w_0 = \mathrm{RN}(w_0 + w_1)$.
    - $\lvert w - x c\rvert \le \eta$.
- **F3.** If every operand is finite and $\lvert x c\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max} - 1}$, then $w_0$ is finite. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max} - 1}$ is $2^{1023}$ for `double`, $2^{127}$ for `float`.
- **F4.** If every operand is finite and $w_0$ is not, then $w = (\pm\infty, 0)$, with the sign of $x c$.
- **F5.** If an operand is not finite, then $w$ is the canonical form of $x_0 \cdot c$ computed in `T`: $(\pm\infty, 0)$ for an infinity, $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$ for a NaN (for example $+\infty \cdot 2 = +\infty$, $0 \cdot \infty = \mathrm{NaN}$).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_pow2_2_full_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeFull.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeFull.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_pow2_2_full_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `mul_pow2_2_full_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** mul_pow2_2, then the fix-up of IEEE-like results (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** core: as mul_pow2_2; fix-up: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_pow2_2_full.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_pow2_2_full.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_pow2_2`](mul_pow2_2.md).

```
# x * c, c a power of two, with IEEE-like results: mul_pow2_2, then the fix-up.
# The fix-up is that of milestone1.md, "IEEE-like results", with r0 = times_inf(t) (exact, so not
# a fused operation) for prod(t, const inf).

(z0, z1) = mul_pow2_2(x0, x1, c)
t        = prod(x0, c)
a        = abs(z0)
f        = lt(a, const inf)
r0       = times_inf(t)
n        = eq(r0, r0)
r1       = select(n, 0, r0)
w0       = select(f, z0, r0)
w1       = select(f, z1, r1)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#mul_pow2_2_full)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)), and the claims of its finite core `mul_pow2_2` on the cases where they apply (F2: finite operands, finite result), which the columns below measure.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound (core `mul_pow2_2`) | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 110 400 000 | 0 | 0.748915 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 110 400 000 | 0 | 0.750000 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 5 484 670 | 0 | 0.746094 (`fp:6:-12:3`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
